case_title.quote: VUTUKURU LAKSHMAIAH v. STATE OF ANDHRA PRADESH
case_title.reason: Case title matches the judgment heading.

number_of_accused.quote: convicted A-1 to A-5 and A-7 to A-9
number_of_accused.reason: Accused numbered A-1 to A-9, so nine accused are supported.

accused_gender.quote: The accused persons took the plea of false implication
accused_gender.reason: Judgment never states the accused's gender; 'Mixed' has no textual basis.

accused_age.reason: No accused age is stated in the judgment.

accused_occupation.quote: Vutukuru Lakshmaiah, A-1, was the Councilor for Ward No. 16 of Nellore Municipality
accused_occupation.reason: Judgment identifies A-1's occupation as Councilor for Ward No. 16.

previous_criminal_record.reason: No accused criminal record is mentioned.

victim_gender.quote: the deceased was assaulted as he was a witness
victim_gender.reason: Victim is referred to with male pronouns throughout.

accused_victim_relationship.correct_value: Known to accused; rival political supporter with previous animosity
accused_victim_relationship.quote: the deceased was assaulted as he was a witness in Velongini Raja's murder case wherein the accused-appellant, A-1, was an accused
accused_victim_relationship.reason: Parties were known rivals with previous animosity, not strangers.

offence_category.reason: Offence is murder under s.302 IPC, as the headnote and judgment state.

statutory_provisions.correct_value: IPC ss. 302, 148, 324, 149 (324 r/w 149); s.307 in FIR; s.304 Part I considered
statutory_provisions.quote: Sections 302 and 148 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC)
statutory_provisions.reason: Omits standalone s.149 and s.307 from the FIR, and the s.304 Part I issue considered.

weapon.quote: A-4 and A-6 beat him with iron rods
weapon.reason: Knives and iron rods are both stated as weapons used.

evidence_type.quote: the testimony of the eye-witnesses-PW 2 and PW 3 and the dying declaration of the victim
evidence_type.reason: Eyewitness testimony and dying declaration are the evidence relied on.

confession.reason: No confession is mentioned; only recoveries at the arrested persons' instance.

aggravating_circumstances.quote: considering the nature of injuries and the previous animosity
aggravating_circumstances.reason: Previous animosity, multiple stab injuries and unlawful assembly are the factors the court relied on.

trial_court_outcome.quote: convicted A-1 to A-5 and A-7 to A-9 for the offences punishable under Sections 148 and 302 IPC
trial_court_outcome.reason: Matches the trial court's convictions as described in the judgment.

high_court_outcome.quote: the High Court has acquitted A-4, A-8 and A-9
high_court_outcome.reason: High Court acquitted A-4, A-8, A-9 and upheld the others' conviction.

final_outcome.quote: we do not perceive any merit in these appeals and accordingly, the same stand dismissed
final_outcome.reason: Supreme Court dismissed appeals, so convictions stand.

offence_finally_established.quote: it is not a fit case where the offence under Section 302 IPC should be converted to Section 304 Part I IPC
offence_finally_established.reason: Offence finally upheld is murder under s.302 IPC.

imprisonment_type.reason: Life imprisonment is the sentence stated.

imprisonment_years.reason: No term in years is stated; the sentence is life.

neutral_facts.correct_value: Same facts without the closing sentence stating the challenges were rejected (that reveals the outcome)
neutral_facts.reason: Facts are accurate, but the final sentence reveals the court outcome, which is prohibited.

offence_severity.correct_value: Life imprisonment imposed under s.302; statutory minimum and maximum not stated
offence_severity.quote: sentenced each of them to suffer rigorous imprisonment for life
offence_severity.reason: Life sentence is supported, but statutory minimum and maximum are not stated in the judgment.

attempt_completion.quote: who succumbed to his injuries three days later
attempt_completion.reason: Victim died, so the offence is completed.

physical_harm.quote: there are five stab injuries at different parts of the body
physical_harm.reason: Multiple stab injuries leading to death three days later are described.

number_of_offences.quote: the appellants ... guilty of the offence under Sections 302 and 148
number_of_offences.reason: Judgment does not state a count of charges; the figures 8 and 7 are not supported.

financial_property_loss.reason: No property or financial loss is discussed.

premeditation_planning.correct_value: Not stated as a premeditation finding; court relied on previous animosity as motive for intent
premeditation_planning.quote: the deceased was assaulted as he was a witness in Velongini Raja's murder case
premeditation_planning.reason: Court relied on previous animosity for intent but did not expressly find premeditation or planning.

motive.quote: considering the nature of injuries and the previous animosity
motive.reason: Previous animosity is the motive identified, linked to the witness status in a murder case.

key_evidence_accepted.quote: the witnesses categorically deposed that they were able to see the accused persons
key_evidence_accepted.reason: Court accepted PW2 and PW3 eyewitness evidence, the dying declaration and witness presence.

witness_credibility.correct_value: Court found witnesses were not chance witnesses and deposed categorically; the 'detailed' testimony point concerns PW-18
witness_credibility.quote: In his testimony, he has categorically stated every aspect in detail
witness_credibility.reason: Credibility finding is right, but the 'detailed testimony' point refers to the Magistrate PW-18, not the eyewitnesses.

trial_duration.correct_value: Offence 14.05.1996; trial court judgment date not stated; High Court judgment 22.03.2007; Supreme Court judgment 24.04.2015
trial_duration.quote: From the Judgment and Order dated 22.03.2007 of the High Court of Andhra Pradesh
trial_duration.reason: 22.03.2007 is the High Court judgment date; the trial court judgment date is not given.

legal_representation.quote: Nagendra Rai, A.T.M. Rangaramanujam, P. N. Ramalingam, for the Appellant
legal_representation.reason: Counsel names for appellant and respondent match the judgment.

investigation_status.quote: the chargesheet was placed before the competent court
investigation_status.reason: Chargesheet filed and trial completed, as the judgment describes.

procedural_irregularity.correct_value: Non-framing of a charge under s.149 IPC was raised; court held no prejudice
procedural_irregularity.quote: the said submission pales into insignificance
procedural_irregularity.reason: Non-framing of the s.149 charge was argued and considered, though found non-prejudicial, so 'None noted' is incomplete.

appeal_history.quote: partly allowed the appeal thereby acquitting A4, A5 and A9
appeal_history.reason: Trial conviction, partial High Court acquittal and Supreme Court dismissal are accurately described.

prosecution_argument.correct_value: State argued dying declaration reliable, witnesses not chance witnesses, s.149 no bar, and not a case for conversion; alibi and intent points are court reasoning
prosecution_argument.quote: there is no reason to discard the dying declaration as there is no infirmity in the same
prosecution_argument.reason: Some points are the State's, but alibi and intent-to-kill arguments are attributed to the prosecution without support.

defence_argument.correct_value: Also argued alibi, no intention to kill, contradictions, and conversion to s.304 Part II
defence_argument.quote: they may be liable for conviction under Section 304 Part II IPC and not under Section 302 IPC
defence_argument.reason: Covers chance witnesses, vague dying declaration and s.149, but omits the alibi, no-intention and s.304 arguments.

legal_principle_applied.quote: the burden shifts to the accused to establish the plea of alibi with certainty
legal_principle_applied.reason: Non-fatal s.149 charge, alibi burden and dying declaration reliability principles are all applied.

precedent_relied_upon.correct_value: Also referred: State of Orissa v. Dibakar Naik; Sunder Lal v. State of Rajasthan; Marimuthu v. State of Tamil Nadu
precedent_relied_upon.quote: State of Orissa v. Dibakar Naik (2002) 5 SCC 323; Sunder Lal v. State of Rajasthan (2007) 10 SCC 371
precedent_relied_upon.reason: Listed precedents are accurate, but three cases referred to in the headnote are omitted.

sentencing_rationale.quote: it is not a fit case where the offence under Section 302 IPC should be converted to Section 304 Part I IPC
sentencing_rationale.reason: No separate sentencing rationale; the only related reasoning concerns conversion, so 'Not applicable' is acceptable.

judicial_mitigating_factors.reason: No mitigating factors were identified by the court.

judicial_aggravating_factors.correct_value: Nature of five stab injuries and previous animosity, relied on to refuse conversion to s.304 Part I
judicial_aggravating_factors.quote: considering the nature of injuries and the previous animosity, we are of the considered opinion
judicial_aggravating_factors.reason: Court expressly relied on injury nature and previous animosity as aggravating; 'None' contradicts this.

other_sentence_order.correct_value: Separate sentence under s.148 IPC imposed; all sentences concurrent
other_sentence_order.quote: imposed separate sentence under Section 148 IPC with the default clause stipulating that all the sentences shall be concurrent
other_sentence_order.reason: Separate s.148 sentence and concurrency direction are stated, so 'None' is wrong.
